title: VONKO-030/ReGALLY: A Resectable GALLbladder and bile duct cancer studY based on real-world data from federal state cancer registries in Germany
summary:
Biliary tract cancers are rare cancers that affect the bile ducts and the gallbladder. They include different types that can develop inside or outside the liver, and these types can behave differently and require different treatments.

Overall, these cancers are uncommon and often have a poor prognosis. Because they are rare, it is difficult to collect strong evidence about the best treatments. Patient numbers are small, and care can vary between hospitals.

If the cancer can be removed, surgery is the main treatment and offers the best chance of cure. However, many patients experience a return of the disease even after surgery. Additional treatments, such as chemotherapy after surgery, may help, but treatment decisions often differ depending on the individual situation.

In everyday medical care, patients may receive different treatments at different times, and recurrences are managed in various ways. However, there is limited information on how patients in Germany are actually treated in routine practice and what outcomes they have.

The ReGALLY study aims to close this gap by analyzing data from cancer registries across Germany. It will examine treatment patterns, timing, and outcomes to better understand current care and identify ways to improve treatment for patients in the future.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of biliary tract

interventions.name: A retrospective analysis of all patients diagnosed with bile duct cancer in Germany between 2005 and 2026.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients
1.   with newly diagnosed BTC (ICD-10 C22.1, C23, C24.0, C24.8, D01.5) from the year of diagnosis 2005 onwards
2.    with Morphology (ICD-O-3): Adenocarcinoma 8140–8149, 8160–8163, 8190–8221, 8250–8552, 8570–8576, 8940–8941, 9110; adenosquamous carcinoma 8560
3.    residing in the relevant federal state at the time of diagnosis
4.    with at least one day of survival / follow-up period
5.    additionally for oBDS-ZfKD and oBDS-LKR (= clinical data):
a.    Year of diagnosis 2020 or later
b.    Resectability approximated via TNM M0 category.
c.    Surgery with curative intent within 6 months of diagnosis 
d.    Surgical outcome: macroscopically complete resection (R0 or R1).
Exclusion criteria:
1.    The case is known to the register solely on the basis of 
a.    a death certificate (DCO case) 
b.    a pathology report 
c.    a follow-up report 
d.	a report to the tumour board 
e.    a combination of the aforementioned report types 
2.    Unknown vital status at the end of the follow-up period
3.    Survival time of 0 days
4.    Additionally for oBDS-ZfKD and oBDS-LKR (= clinical data):
a.    Unresectable BTC
